notes.A: The long counter and checkerboard floor establish the diner, but the bare wall dominates.
notes.B: Foreground rats have real presence, but the close crop cuts out the seating.
notes.C: The tables and both counters explain the layout, but the rats are easy to miss.
notes.D: A rat, a can and hanging pans set the scene, but the near wall crowds it.
notes.E: The cleaver and rats suggest what’s on the menu, but the seating is mostly cropped.
notes.F: The aisle shows how the counters fit together, but the window draws attention past them.
notes.G: The rats stand out on the metal counter, but the tight view loses the diner.
notes.H: Stools, tables and rat-covered counters tell the whole story, though the rats are small.

ratdogs.best: The stools, tables, rat-covered counters and hanging pans show the diner and its infestation in one frame.
ratdogs.lacks: The prep area lacks a recognizable cooking station. The rats give it character, but the plain counters give them little context.
ratdogs.fix: Replace the gray prep island with a grease-stained flat-top grill, with a rat carcass on the cooking surface.

blind_name.name: Diner counter
blind_name.why: A wooden service counter, red stools, round tables, checkerboard flooring, and hanging pans suggest a diner.
blind_name.odd: The objects on the counter are hard to identify.
